name: Limitless
tagline: Personalized AI memory via wearable and desktop
description: Limitless AI was a memory-capture platform built around a wearable pendant and desktop app that transcribed and summarized conversations and meetings. Meta acquired Limitless in December 2025, stopped selling the pendant, and began winding the service down through 2026. GAIA is a proactive productivity OS that manages your email, calendar, tasks, and workflows across 50+ integrations — no hardware required — and it is actively maintained.
metaTitle: Limitless vs GAIA: Memory That Takes Action
metaDescription: Limitless was acquired by Meta in December 2025 and is winding down. GAIA is a living, source-available alternative that triages email, manages tasks, and runs workflows across 50+ tools.
intro: Limitless AI built its reputation on a compelling idea: a wearable pendant that passively recorded and transcribed everything you said throughout the day, giving you a searchable memory of every meeting and conversation. In December 2025 Meta acquired Limitless, stopped selling the pendant, and began winding the service down through 2026, with support promised for existing owners for at least a year. Memory capture was only ever the starting line. GAIA operates at a different layer entirely — it does not just remember your conversations, it acts on them. GAIA reads your inbox, triages emails by urgency, drafts replies, creates tasks from context, prepares meeting briefings, and executes multi-step automations across 50+ tools. Where Limitless augmented your recall, GAIA augments your output. And it does all of this without requiring you to buy, charge, or wear any hardware.

rows.gaia: Proactive AI productivity OS that monitors email, calendar, and connected tools and executes actions across your digital life on your behalf
rows.competitor: Passive memory capture platform: records, transcribes, and summarizes spoken conversations via a wearable pendant and desktop app

rows.gaia: Graph-based persistent memory built from structured integrations: connects tasks to emails, meetings to people, and projects to outcomes; learns behavioral patterns over time
rows.competitor: Captures in-person and virtual conversations through the pendant or a desktop recording agent; stores searchable transcripts and AI-generated summaries queryable via a chat interface

rows.gaia: Full Gmail automation: reads and triages by urgency, drafts context-aware replies, auto-labels, creates tasks from emails, and drives inbox-zero workflows
rows.competitor: No active email management; can surface email context when querying conversation history, but does not read, triage, draft, or act on inbox messages

rows.gaia: AI-powered todo management with semantic search, labels, priorities, projects, deadlines, and automatic task creation from email, conversation, or meeting notes
rows.competitor: Can identify action items mentioned in recorded meetings and suggest them post-summary; no dedicated task system, project hierarchy, or deadline tracking

rows.gaia: Multi-step automations described in natural language with triggers, conditions, and cross-tool actions spanning email, calendar, Slack, Notion, GitHub, and more
rows.competitor: No workflow automation engine; core function is capture and recall, not execution or cross-tool orchestration

rows.gaia: Fully software-based: runs on web, desktop (all operating systems), mobile, and CLI with no physical device required
rows.competitor: Pendant sales stopped in December 2025 after Meta’s acquisition; existing owners were promised at least a year of continued support

rows.gaia: 50+ integrations via MCP including Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear, Todoist, Asana, ClickUp, and Jira with deep bi-directional actions
rows.competitor: Integrates with Zoom, Google Meet, and other video conferencing tools for virtual meeting capture; limited broader tool ecosystem

rows.gaia: Source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial) and self-hostable via Docker: your data never leaves your own infrastructure; no training on user data when self-hosted
rows.competitor: Closed-source proprietary platform; consent-first design with per-conversation recording controls; continuing users fall under Meta’s privacy terms, and service ended in the EU, UK, Brazil, and other regions

Multi-step workflow automation with natural-language triggers spanning 50+ integrated tools

verdict: Limitless AI excelled at one thing — giving you a searchable memory of your spoken conversations through a wearable device. It is now winding down under Meta, with hardware sales stopped and service promised only through 2026. If you want an AI that runs your digital life end-to-end — triaging email, executing calendar actions, automating multi-step workflows across 50+ integrations, and doing all of it in software, on any device, with full data ownership — GAIA is built for that, and it is actively maintained.

faqs.question: Can GAIA replace the Limitless pendant for meeting capture?
faqs.answer: GAIA handles virtual meeting intelligence through calendar integration — preparing pre-meeting briefings, capturing action items from meeting notes, and creating tasks automatically. It does not record ambient in-person audio the way the Limitless pendant does. If passive recording of face-to-face conversations is critical for you, the pendant addresses that specific gap. For everything else — inbox management, task automation, workflow execution, and cross-tool orchestration — GAIA covers ground that Limitless never reaches.

faqs.question: Limitless was acquired by Meta in late 2025 — what does that mean for users?
faqs.answer: Meta acquired Limitless in December 2025 and halted new hardware sales. Existing customers were moved to an unlimited plan and given one year of continued support. The long-term product direction under Meta is uncertain. GAIA is source-available (PolyForm Noncommercial) and self-hostable, meaning there is no acquisition risk — you can run it on your own infrastructure indefinitely, independent of any company's strategic decisions.

faqs.question: How does GAIA's memory compare to Limitless's memory system?
faqs.answer: Limitless builds memory from audio: it records what you say, transcribes it, and lets you search the transcript archive. GAIA builds memory from structured integrations: it connects tasks to the emails that created them, links meetings to the people who attended them, and tracks project outcomes across your tool stack using a graph-based memory model. These are complementary approaches — Limitless excels at conversational recall, while GAIA excels at understanding and acting on the relationships between your work, your tools, and your time.
